correctness.rationale: The graph is the intact 25-vertex Cartesian product, with sum of cyclic coordinate distances. A three-point set is forbidden exactly when its largest pair distance is the sum of the other two; the no-forbidden-triple property is hereditary. Increasing extensions exhaust every admissible set, and the absence of seven-vertex faces rules out all greater sizes. In X and Y the ordinary boundary columns delete one vertex over F_2; the relative basis consists of faces containing the discarded vertex, and deletion of that vertex gives zero in the quotient. The fresh exhaustive calculation gives f_X=(25,300,1400,2450,1360,50), f_Y=(24,276,1232,2058,1088,38), f_rel=(1,24,168,392,272,12), and positive-degree boundary ranks X=(24,276,1074,1290,50), Y=(23,253,935,1038,38), and relative=(1,23,139,241,12). Subtract adjacent ranks (and the degree-zero augmentation when reduced) to get all displayed Betti numbers and the other vanishing. To cross-check the natural-map ranks without choosing coordinate cycles, exactness gives b_rel(j)=b_X(j)-rank(i_j)+b_Y(j-1)-rank(i_(j-1)). Starting from degree zero gives 44,74,12 in degrees 2–4 and forces zero outside. This matches the independent direct quotient-of-cycle-span computation. The degree-three kernel and cokernel have dimensions 85-74=11 and 86-74=12. Translations of the intact graph give the identical result for any deleted landmark.
residual_risks: This is exhaustive for the stated finite complex and coefficients, not evidence for integral torsion, a homotopy type, larger products, or a graph-vertex deletion that recomputes shortest paths.

evidence: The Cartesian-product paper treats the maximum cardinality of a general-position set on cylinders and tori. General Position Polynomials counts faces of each size, and its Cartesian-product formulas examined concern products of paths.

evidence: X is the independence complex of the 3-uniform hypergraph of graph-geodesically collinear triples; Y is the induced deletion in that same hypergraph. For its vertex link L, adjoining the missing vertex amounts to adjoining the cone on L; relative homology is the shifted reduced homology of L.

Related studies found for geodesic general-position sets concern extremal sizes or other graph products, and the nearby indexed Vietoris–Rips result concerns a pairwise distance bound rather than this forbidden-triple condition.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: There are no missing edges in X, but there are forbidden triples, so this is not a nontrivial Rips complex at any scale (Rips complexes are flag). Computing only the full space up to homotopy, or the maximum-size sets, also would not specify the inclusion with this fixed induced deletion.

value.rationale: The graph is a small nontrivial symmetric toroidal grid; retaining the ambient metric while removing one site is the natural induced vertex-deletion operation on the geodesic complex. The result quantifies an actual failure of homological persistence: a change from 85 to 86 in the middle Betti number hides eleven lost independent classes and twelve new ones. Knowing the complete inclusion and relative data is materially more informative for this example than an isolated Betti census or the already studied maximum face size.
residual_risks: One fixed metric and one field; general robustness or geometric conclusions beyond this exact example remain unproved.
